anomalies.observed: The M-BUS connectors J1 and J2 show the +5V net on pin 25 (the left-hand label rows read PIN1, PORTB2, PIN5, +3V3, PORTB1, PIN11, PIN13, TXD2, PIN17, PWM1_C1, PWM1_C2, PIN23, +5V, PIN27, BAT), i.e. +5V is tied to bus pin 25 while pin 27 is left as the generic unconnected 'PIN27'.
anomalies.expected: The +5V rail must be tied to the M5Stack bus's 5V pin, which the specification places at pin 27: "The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin)". On the M5Stack bus the 5V pins are 27/28 (pin 25 is a GPIO), so connecting +5V to pin 25 both fails to pick up the bus 5V supply and applies 5V to a GPIO.

evidence.quote: The same `+5V` net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin), so `+5V` is effectively the logical OR of "M5Stack-supplied 5V" and "external 5V input via D1".
J2/J1 left-column labels: ... PIN23, +5V, PIN27, BAT (rows 23, 25, 27, 29) — +5V sits on the pin-25 row, while pin 27 is labelled PIN27.

anomalies.impact: The board would not receive 5V from the M5Stack bus (the real 5V pin 27 is unused), so the servo rail (fed from +5V via D2) would be unpowered when relying on the Core supply, and the 5V rail would instead be driven onto a bus GPIO (pin 25), risking damage to that ESP32 pin.

parsed.summary: All component values, types and diode orientations match the specification, but the +5V rail appears to be tied to M-BUS pin 25 rather than the M5Stack 5V pin 27 that the specification calls out, which would starve the servo rail of bus power and put 5V on a GPIO; the finding is low-confidence because the small pin-number text on J1/J2 is hard to read with certainty.
